## Overview

The semester-long applied project is completed in partnership with the [Northern Border Regional Commission (NBRC)](https://www.nbrc.gov), a federal-state economic and community development commission serving rural northern Maine, New Hampshire, New York, and Vermont.

Students work in small teams. Each team analyzes a different **domain area** across NBRC's full four-state territory (rather than each team covering a single state). All teams use a consistent structure so outputs are comparable and can be assembled into a unified product for NBRC.

---

## Domain Areas

For now, teams will be organized around two domain areas (more may be added before Week 7 if enrollment supports it):

- *Rural Housing*: issues relating to supply, demand, and affordability of housing in NBRC counties
- *Rural Hub Services*: quantifying and visualizing the essential businesses or amenities that appear in central regional towns to serve all the smaller surrounding communities

## Deliverable Format

*[Draft — instructor to revise as project scope firms up after the Week 6 kickoff.]*

Each of the four graded milestones below builds directly on the last. There's no single "project" handed in at the end, just a steady accumulation of the same deliverable getting more complete and more polished.

### Scope & Team Charter (Week 7, 10%)

A short planning document, not an analysis. At this point in the semester, teams have core R/tidyverse skills but haven't yet covered spatial analysis (Weeks 8–9) or Quarto (Week 10). Should include:

- Team roster and a rough division of responsibilities
- The domain area (Rural Housing or Rural Hub Services) and 2–3 concrete research questions the team plans to answer for NBRC
- A first pass at data sources (ACS, BLS, USDA ERS, TIGER shapefiles, possible NBRC-provided data)
- A work plan mapped to the remaining milestones below

Must be a Quarto document (`.qmd`). The point at this stage is alignment within the team and with the instructor, not production value.

### Preliminary Outputs + Peer Critique (Week 12, 20%)

By this point teams have covered spatial analysis and Quarto, so this milestone should look like real, if rough, output. Expect to bring:

- At least one polished chart or map addressing one of your research questions, built in R (`ggplot2`/`sf`)
- A short written or verbal framing of what the visualization shows and why it matters to NBRC
- Participation in structured peer critique, giving and receiving feedback with at least one other team in class

This is graded on effort and communication quality, not on having "finished" analysis. The critique is meant to catch problems while there's still time to fix them.

### Draft Deliverable + Revision (Week 14, 20%)

A near-complete version of the final deliverable: full narrative structure, multiple visualizations/maps, and a clear throughline connecting data to a recommendation or insight for NBRC. Submitted for instructor feedback, with in-class time for revision afterward. Should be built in Quarto, with the team's choice of report, slide deck, or simple dashboard, consistent with what's covered in Week 10.

### Final Deliverable + Presentation (Week 16, 20%)

This is the polished, NBRC-facing version of the Draft Deliverable, incorporating Week 14 feedback. It's a Quarto-rendered report, dashboard, or slide deck that could credibly be handed to NBRC staff. Delivered in person in Montpelier alongside a short team presentation to NBRC stakeholders. All teams follow the same general structure so the final outputs can be assembled into one unified product across domain areas.
